newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Power NZ news sends NZ shares to a weaker close.
newsitem.headline: Power NZ news sends NZ shares to a weaker close.

text.p: * Power NZ share price slump forces top-40 index lower close
* Otherwise, market flat on moderate volume
* Telecom up on share buyback
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index -12.17 at 2,295.39
134 nil * NZSC cap index +11.13 at 5,010.88
316 -6 * NZMC .NZMC cap index -3.07 at 1,858.99
356 +1 * Volume NZ$54.3 million. Futures -5 at 1,155
669 +5 * Other movers - -155
The New Zealand sharemarket closed weaker on Tuesday after news that two major shareholders of electricity company Power New Zealand were joining forces and would offer NZ$6 per share to minorities.

Utilicorp NZ, a unit of Utilicorp United Inc, and unlisted Mercury Energy ended a long-running battle for control of Power NZ when they announced they were forming a joint venture to hold their respective shareholdings.
Shares in Power NZ, New Zealand's second largest electricity company, slumped $1.55 to $6.50, with just 200 shares traded.
"That accounted for 11.1 of the down-points of the NZSE-40 today," said Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch.
The NZSE-40 Capital Index closed 12.17 points weaker at 2,295.39.

However, brokers said the market could have been worse off had Telecom not ended six cents firmer at $6.70. The second stage of the market leader's $1 billion share buyback continued to buoy the stock.
There had been selling in selected shares, among them Fletcher Paper, which closed six cents weaker at $3.16, and Fisher & Paykel, down 12 cents at $5.00.
Brokers said the immediate focus was the U.S. FOMC meeting tonight (NZT). Opinion was divided on whether the Federal Reserve will raise short-term interest rates at its policy meeting.
-- Matthew Brockett, Wellington newsroom (64 4) 471 4275
